summaries.body:
The 5.0 mapping records V13.1.1 as modified and moved from 4.0.3 V1.1.5, which asked for a security analysis of the application's high-level architecture and all connected remote services. The current clause is narrower: document communication needs, including relied-upon external services and cases where an end user can supply an external location. The mapping itself notes that the predecessor text is dissimilar and that git/content lineage diverges from the ID slot, so the mapping and V1.1.5 wording are the reliable origin.

That architecture framing was already under debate before 4.0 shipped. In August 2018 ossie-git opened issue 274 on the V1 architecture chapter; Andrew van der Stock wrote on 2 October 2018 that the section needed a solid rewrite and that it was unclear which components counted as part of the application versus external services. Git events stamped V13.1.1 (vanderaj's 1 January 2019 malicious-code refactor, abhay's 11 February 2019 CWE pass, and the 26 February 2019 #513 encoding fix) belong to an earlier API/malicious occupant of this number and do not attest this documentation control.

While the control still lived as V1.1.5, Josh Grossman made minor V1 tweaks on 10 February 2019 and mb reworded 1.x.x on 12 February 2019. The 5.0 mapping then records a modification that drops the high-level architecture analysis and asks instead that communication needs—including user-provided external locations—be documented.

The rest of the attached timeline is ID-slot reuse after the 4.0 chapter shuffle: moving SSRF out of deserialization, CWE tagging on Malicious/API, cookie __Host- prefixes, and issue 513 (mismatched encoding / URL parsers), which vanderaj resolved against a then-current V13.1.1 on 26 February 2019. Those commits did not rewrite this configuration-documentation clause.
